summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -3 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; risk −; energy 0; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +4.8%; weakest: Lean hogs -22.5%. Key releases ahead: US Core CPI m/m (11-10 8:30 AM ET); US CPI m/m (11-10 8:30 AM ET); US Core PPI m/m (11-13 8:30 AM ET); US PPI m/m (11-13 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.86% (-42 bp in a month), 2-year 4.51% (-26 bp); 2s10s curve +35 bp (-16 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.00% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.88 (-0.3% in a month, +3.7% YTD). USD/BRL 5.509 (+9.8% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.661 (-0.6%); USD/MXN 18.60 (+2.3%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -5.4% in a month (+7.8% YTD); VIX 23.4. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 88.36 $/bbl (-2.9% in a month), Brent 95.03, ULSD 4.293 $/gal (-6.4%), natural gas 3.06 (-13.8%). Crude little changed on the month. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -5.5% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.0%, Hang Seng +1.0%, yuan +0.6% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 6 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (18%); S&P GSCI -6.9% in a month; gold -2.2%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
